requirements.requirement: Provide an encrypted volume mounted at /srv/secure on node1
requirements.summary: A LUKS2-encrypted, file-backed volume was created (luksFormat/luksOpen), formatted with XFS, and mounted at /srv/secure; df/mount output confirms 944M available and correct mount point.

requirements.requirement: Volume unlocks and mounts automatically at boot without manual intervention
requirements.summary: crypttab and fstab entries were added with a root-only keyfile; a pre-reboot healthy baseline (boot_id 71f12f87..., mounted volume, test data) was captured; systemctl reboot was issued and acknowledged; the node became unreachable then returned with a different boot_id (e4ca3021...), directly proving a real restart; post-reboot state shows /srv/secure mounted via /dev/mapper/srv-secure, systemd-cryptsetup@srv-secure.service active/succeeded, cryptsetup status confirming the LUKS2 mapping, and the test file content intact — all without any manual cryptsetup or mount command issued after reboot.

overall_summary: The executor built a LUKS2 encrypted file-backed volume mounted at /srv/secure and configured crypttab/fstab plus a keyfile for unattended unlock. Critically, it directly demonstrated the full availability transition required for a boot-time requirement: healthy pre-reboot baseline, an actual reboot (boot_id changed from 71f12f87... to e4ca3021..., matching the fixed lifecycle snapshots), and a fully recovered post-reboot state with the volume auto-unlocked, mounted, service active, and test data intact — with no manual commands run after reboot. Both material outcomes are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence.
limitations: No independent restart-evidence protocol beyond this single task-driven reboot was reported separately; however, since the task itself requires boot behavior, the one observed reboot cycle directly serves as the required transition evidence.
Only one reboot cycle was captured; repeated reboots or crash-consistency scenarios were not tested, though not required by the task.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command trace shows a coherent sequence: OS/package discovery, cryptsetup install, backing file + keyfile creation, luksFormat/luksOpen, XFS mkfs and manual mount test, close and crypttab/fstab configuration, generated-unit start and mount -a validation, pre-reboot baseline capture, controlled reboot, and post-reboot verification. Every state-changing command maps directly to building or validating the required outcome; the manual mapping was closed before reboot testing rather than left open redundantly. The only residue is /tmp/reboot.log, an incidental artifact of the backgrounded reboot command with negligible footprint and no security or functional impact. No abandoned experiments, conflicting services, or unnecessary broad mutations were observed; package-health and failed-services checks remain clean before and after.
